<!-- plain-summary -->
This is the core of the switch: a new module that stores Wyrd's bookkeeping data in FoundationDB instead of TiKV. It plugs into the same internal interface the current backends use, and it must pass the exact same test suite they do — so from the rest of the system's point of view, nothing changes but the name of the database.

## What

New crate `crates/metadata-fdb` implementing `MetadataStore` (`crates/traits/src/lib.rs:338`) on the [`foundationdb`](https://crates.io/crates/foundationdb) crate (0.10.x — the community wrapper over the official `libfdb_c` client, BindingTester-validated upstream). Feature-gated like the TiKV driver (`--features fdb`), routed through the shared conformance suite's `run_all`.

## Semantics mapping (the heart of the work)

FDB is optimistic where TiKV is pessimistic; the arbiter is the trait + shared `metadata-conformance` suite as they stand — evolving implementation-first alongside this work (any suite change keeps `redb`/`tikv` green in the same PR), consolidated afterwards in #437.

| Contract operation | FDB mapping |
|---|---|
| `get` / `scan` | Single read-only transaction; snapshot-consistent for free. `scan(prefix)` → range read over the prefix range. |
| `commit(batch)` — preconditions | Inside one FDB transaction: read each `require`/`require_absent` key (a plain read — this adds it to the **read-conflict set**); if the value check fails, return `Ok(Conflict)` without writing. |
| `commit(batch)` — mutations | Buffer `put`/`delete` in the same transaction; commit. |
| Lost race on a **conditional** batch | Commit fails with error **1020 `not_committed`** (a conflicting write landed on a read-conflict key) → classify as `Ok(Conflict)`, mirroring `conflict_or_err`'s `conditional = !batch.preconditions.is_empty()` rule in the TiKV driver. |
| **Blind** batch | No reads → empty read-conflict set → blind writes cannot conflict in FDB; any commit error is a genuine `Err`, never `Conflict`. Matches the contract: blind batches must not swallow failures as `Conflict`. |
| **1021 `commit_unknown_result`** | Never blind-retry: `WriteBatch` is not guaranteed idempotent. Surface as a distinguishable error — one of the contract points #437 consolidates after this lands. (Follow-up headroom: versionstamped idempotency keys, only if operations show this error class matters in practice.) |
| Retry policy | Bounded retry of 1020-class **retryable** errors for read paths and blind batches where safe; conditional batches return `Conflict` and let callers (e.g. `alloc_inode`'s budgeted backoff loop) decide. Do NOT use the crate's `db.run` closure-retry blindly — it re-runs on 1021. |

## Envelope

Single `WriteBatch` commits are far inside FDB's 5 s / 10 MB transaction limits and 10 KB/100 KB key/value limits; an envelope check in the shared suite (added here or at the #437 consolidation) asserts our fixtures stay there. No transaction spanning multiple `commit` calls exists in the trait — good.

## Config

- Cluster file path via `WYRD_FDB_CLUSTER_FILE` (default `/etc/foundationdb/fdb.cluster`), mirroring `WYRD_TIKV_PD_ENDPOINTS` precedent in `crates/server/src/cli.rs`.
- The client requires a one-time `foundationdb::boot()`/network-thread start; own that inside the driver's constructor with a process-global guard (the C client allows exactly one network thread per process).

## Acceptance criteria

- `metadata-fdb` passes all 7 conformance contracts via `run_all` against a real `fdbserver` (docker), including `contract_rename_race_yields_conflict` and both precondition contracts.
- A driver-level test for the blind-batch/`Err` rule and one forcing 1020 classification (two clients racing on a `require`d key).
- `cargo build` without the `fdb` feature is unaffected (no `libfdb_c` link demand on default builds).

## Sequencing

Depends on #436 (decision — done, ADR-0042 merged). #437 is a follow-on consolidation, not a prerequisite (implementation-first per ADR-0002): this issue is now the head of the FDB track. Blocks: CI harness, server selection, packaging, and the go/no-go battery. Targets `main` after `feat/m4-production-metadata-backend` merges.

milestone.title: Metadata Store FoundationDB
milestone.description: Production distributed MetadataStore backend on FoundationDB — the chosen production backend per ADR-0042. metadata-fdb behind the fdb feature (implementation-first per ADR-0002; contract docs consolidated afterwards in #437), libfdb_c packaging + wyrd:fdb image, dev/CI harness, deploy profiles, go/no-go fault+contention battery, and the TiKV development stand-down once FDB is the default. (Renamed from metadata-client.)
